title: Charlotte royale
subtitle: The domed French dessert lined with Swiss roll spirals and filled with bavarian cream
excerpt: Charlotte royale is a dome-shaped dessert: a pudding basin lined with slices of jam Swiss roll so the spiral pattern covers the outside, filled with a set bavarian cream, and unmoulded to serve. The spiral pattern is the point. The bavarian cream inside needs gelatine to hold its shape when unmoulded.
sourceNotes: Charlotte royale is attributed to the French chef Marie-Antoine Careme, who is thought to have created it in the early nineteenth century. It is distinguished from charlotte russe (which uses savoiardi to line the mould) by its Swiss roll lining. The recipe as described here follows the standard published technique for home patisserie.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before. Chill overnight and unmould just before serving. The Swiss roll slices are easier to cut once the cream has set fully.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Swiss roll sponge only. Conventional oven, 200 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 185 degrees Celsius. The sponge bakes in 10 to 12 minutes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A set cream made from creme anglaise (egg yolk, milk, and sugar cooked together until thickened) mixed with dissolved gelatine and then folded with whipped cream. It sets firm enough to unmould cleanly but remains light and tender when eaten.

content.text: Charlotte royale is assembled in two stages: first the Swiss roll lining, then the

filling. The Swiss roll must be tight, evenly rolled, and completely cold before slicing. The bavarian cream must be on the edge of setting (cool enough to thicken but not yet firm) before it goes into the lined bowl, or it will flow under the sponge slices and the spirals will slip out of position.

Preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius. Line a large flat baking tray (32 x 22 cm approximately) with baking paper. Whisk the eggs and caster sugar together over a bain-marie until thick and mousse-like, then remove from heat and whisk until cool. Fold in the flour and spread onto the tray.

Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until just set and lightly golden. Turn out onto a fresh sheet of baking paper dusted with caster sugar. Peel off the lining paper. Spread with raspberry jam and roll up tightly from the short end while still warm. Cool completely, then chill for 1 hour.
Line a 1.2 litre pudding basin with cling film. Slice the Swiss roll into 1.5 cm slices and press them tightly against the sides and base of the bowl, spiral side facing outward, with no gaps.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water for 5 minutes

content.text: Heat the milk with the vanilla pod and seeds until steaming. Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together until pale. Pour the hot milk slowly onto the yolk mixture, whisking constantly. Return to the saucepan and stir over low heat until the mixture coats the back of a spoon (82 to 84 degrees Celsius). Remove from heat.

Squeeze the soaked gelatine leaves to remove excess water. Add them to the hot custard and stir until dissolved. Strain through a fine sieve into a clean bowl. Cool over ice water, stirring occasionally, until the custard is the consistency of double cream and just starting to thicken at the edges (about 18 to 20 degrees Celsius).
Fold the whipped cream into the thickened custard in two additions. Pour into the lined bowl. Cover with any remaining Swiss roll slices to seal the base. Chill for at least 6 hours or overnight.

Place a flat plate over the top of the basin and invert in one confident movement. The cling film will release the charlotte from the bowl. Peel the cling film away carefully and serve immediately or return to the fridge for up to 1 hour.
